IV (Testing the method): The few parameter choice adopted in Ref. 54 is used only to initialize the present most general 8W + 1 (by including also the optimization of H_MF(alpha) and Delta tau) parameter ansatz |psi_tau>. || Sec. V: in order to compare the stripe with periodicity W = 8 and W = 7 and the uniform d-wave solution, calculations on a 16 x 16 and 14 x 16 clusters are carried out with 16 x 16 different twists in the BZ. || Sec. VI: For this reason for U/t = 2 (U/t = 4) a much larger mesh for the TABC was used with 64 x 64 (32 x 32) different twists in the BZ, instead of the smaller 16 x 16 grid used for U/t = 8 and U/t = 6. [...] much larger cluster simulations are prohibitive at present. || Fig. 11 caption: [...] at the lowest T_eff (i.e. largest tau t = 4, 2.6, 1.73, 1.3 for U/t = 2, 4, 6, 8, respectively) and 16 x 16 cluster. [...] In these calculations, in order to reduce at most the stochastic bias, at each iteration a quite large number (> 3 x 10^5) of samples for evaluating energy derivatives was used [...] || Sec. V (half filling): However, tau t <= 1.3 has been chosen also in this case, in order to show the strength of this approach even when short time projections are employed. || Acknowledgments: I acknowledge PRACE for awarding access to Marconi at CINECA Italy, and Riken collaboration for access to HOKUSAI supercomputer in Saitama Japan.

compute.note: Ansatz for this row is not identified in the worklist beyond 'VAFQMC' (half-filling or small-cluster benchmark entries from the Supplementary Information); the paper states a four (three) parameter uniform ansatz at finite doping and antiferromagnetic order allowed at half filling, and tau t <= 1.3 at half filling, but no parameter count is attributed to this specific entry, so parameters is null. Worklist row cites the journal URL (PRB 107, 115133, 2023) = arXiv:2101.07045 (S. Sorella, VAFQMC). No run time, core count, core-hours or per-run sample count is stated for any energy in the paper; the only sample statement (> 3 x 10^5 samples per optimisation iteration) is given for the uniform d-wave ansatz optimisation of Fig. 11 on 16 x 16, not for the stripe runs, so samples is left null. Cost-relevant settings that are stated: twist-averaged boundary conditions with 16 x 16 twists for U/t = 8 and 6 (32 x 32 for U/t = 4, 64 x 64 for U/t = 2, in the uniform-phase study); projection time tau t = 1.3 (U/t = 8), 1.73 (U/t = 6), 2.6 (U/t = 4) at the lowest T_eff; a single Trotter step parameter Delta tau optimised. Hardware only as acknowledgements (Marconi/CINECA via PRACE, HOKUSAI/RIKEN). Individual filling/U energies are tabulated in the Supplementary Information, not in the main arXiv text.

corrections.reason: The cited paper did not produce the number and does not contain it: PRA 92, 033603 is the method paper, attached two years after the upload in answer to a request for 'a paper describing the AFQMC method with negative U' (PR #23 thread). The energy is VarBench's own computation, run by co-author Yiqi Yang (Zhang group) with AFQMCLAB and described in the VarBench paper's Suppl. S3 E 1-2. Same history and same fix as the sibling repulsive row Hubbard/square_64_P_32_8 AFQMC -33.642(5), whose reference was changed to the Science paper under the 2026-09-21 ruling (option a, corrections.mjs 'FP4-arxiv-2507-02644#2'); this entry applies that precedent to the eleven rows listed in qmbl-verify DECISIONS.md section 1 as '11 Hubbard (PRA 92, 033603) | the cited paper is a dilute continuum gas study', whose ruling (2026-09-16) was on hold because 'the premise is not established'; the PR #23 exchange (the uploader naming PRA 92 as the method paper) and the VarBench SM's own description of these runs establish it. This is a reference change only, not the rejected baseline/contributed flag. Energy, sigma and bound_type stay: the run is sign-problem-free (N_up = N_dn = 32 in the trial determinant, half filling, bipartite lattice), extrapolated to dt -> 0, so exact (stochastic) with its sigma.
